Autoconf’s `install-sh` originates from the X Window System:

- **Original source:** `X11R5`, specifically `mit/util/scripts/install.sh`.
- **Later release:** It was released in **X11R6** as `xc/config/util/install.sh`.
- **Current attribution:** The X11R6-derived version carries **Copyright (C) 1994 X Consortium**, under an MIT-style license. It also states that **FSF changes are in the public domain**.  
  Source: [Autoconf `build-aux/install-sh`](https://fossies.org/linux/autoconf/build-aux/install-sh)

Older Autoconf/Automake copies carried a different notice: **“Copyright 1991 by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology”**, with an advertising clause. Automake changed the notice to the X Consortium copyright and license in a 2003 commit, removing that clause.  
Source: [bug-autoconf discussion](https://lists.nongnu.org/archive/html/bug-autoconf/2018-09/msg00009.html)

The Autoconf 2.13 manual described `install-sh` as being “from the X Consortium” and “not copyrighted,” but that statement predates the later copyright notice.  
Source: [Autoconf 2.13 manual](http://odysseus.fi.muni.cz/pub/gnu/old-gnu/Manuals/autoconf-2.13/html_node/autoconf%5F84.html)
